clue.text: Boxes and case ultimately not packed together

parts.note: to box is to spar, so boxes gives spars

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word case

explanation.surface: A removal job where boxes and a case have ultimately been left unpacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' reads as cartons, but it is the verb: a fighter who boxes spars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse things are thinly scattered, the opposite of crowded or densely packed.

clue.text: Maybe posh ladies' rings pursuing policeman left

indicators.note: pursuing means the rings come after the policeman and left

parts.note: a super is a police superintendent
two rings are two Os

explanation.surface: Rings belonging to some posh ladies are left behind as they chase a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies'' is the British word for a women's toilet; 'Maybe' warns this is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A superloo is a smart, upmarket public lavatory, so a posh ladies' room is one example.

clue.text: Article and paper under debate

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
tissue is thin paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper article being argued over.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point being disputed or discussed.

clue.text: Irish stew with latte almost causing one to tuck in?

indicators.note: a stew mixes things up, so the letters are jumbled
almost means the last letter of latte is dropped

explanation.surface: Irish stew with a coffee nearly makes someone tuck in to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' shuffles IRISH with LATT (latte less its last letter, 'almost'). 'tuck in' suggests eating; a shirt tail is what gets tucked in.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail of a shirt is the part pushed into the trousers, tucked in.

clue.text: Invite ill pro to appear in a parody

indicators.note: the word for pro is to appear inside the word for parody

parts.note: a skit is a short comic parody
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: An ailing professional is being invited to appear in a comic send-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invite ill' reads as asking a sick person along; here it means to court trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for it is an idiom for provoking trouble, inviting harm upon yourself.

clue.text: Relation going on about best friend needing a groom?

definitions.text: Relation going on about best friend needing a groom?

parts.words: Relation going on about best friend needing a groom?
parts.note: a long rambling relation, or tale, about man's best friend in want of a good brushing

explanation.walkthrough: A relation is a story told; a dog is man's best friend, and an unkempt one needs grooming. The phrase means a long joke with a feeble punchline.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-winded tale with a pointless ending is named after jokes about a hairy hound.

clue.text: What dentist may give you that's suffered in endless grief?

parts.note: grief with no end has lost its final letter, the F

explanation.surface: A dentist hands something to a patient who has suffered through endless grief.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as F-LOSS: that is what 'grief' suffers when it is made 'endless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists hand out dental thread for cleaning between teeth.

clue.text: Stick outfit on old composer

parts.note: a rod is a stick
a rig is an outfit of clothing

explanation.surface: Sticking an outfit on an old composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Joaquin Rodrigo was the Spanish composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez.

clue.text: Chap in time, I'm relieved to hear, for select group

parts.note: he is a male person, a chap

indicators.note: to hear says the exclamation is taken by its sound

parts.note: phew is the exclamation of someone relieved

explanation.surface: A man arrives just in time, to everyone's relief, for an exclusive group.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls Churchill's tribute to the RAF pilots of the Battle of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The few is a phrase for a small, chosen band, as in Churchill's praise of RAF pilots.

clue.text: Hear of TV host — he's dashed fancy!

indicators.note: dashed means smashed or thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone hears about a TV presenter, and he is rather fancy!
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed' rearranges HEAR OF TV HOST HE; the S of 'he's' is spare, as solvers noted on the blog.
explanation.definitionFit: To have the hots for someone is slang for being sexually attracted to them.

clue.text: One fussy serviceman dropped round to see mother for first time

parts.note: fussy, prudish behaviour is prim
the Roman numeral for one is I
a para is a paratrooper, a soldier dropped by parachute

explanation.surface: A fussy soldier calls round to visit his mother for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped round' looks like a casual visit, but 'dropped' belongs to the paratrooper and 'round to see' is linking. 'One' sits after 'fussy' in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A primipara is the medical term for a woman giving birth to her first child.

clue.text: School diet includes no chicken

indicators.note: includes says the answer is held within the words school diet

explanation.surface: A school menu with no chicken on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no chicken' is short for 'no spring chicken', someone no longer young.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is no spring chicken is getting on in years, an elderly person.

clue.text: Irish broadcasters carrying round TV for a favour

indicators.note: carrying says the Irish broadcasters hold the other pieces inside

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster
a round shape is the letter O
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: Irish broadcasters bringing a television round as a favour to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favour' is not a kindness but the old sense of a badge or ribbon worn to show support.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon or badge worn as a token of allegiance, as a rosette is at a show or election.

clue.text: Glower, making yak kick out

parts.note: to yak is to chatter, to gas
to kick someone out of a job is to fire them

explanation.surface: Someone scowls, which makes their yak kick out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' reads as a scowl, but it is literally 'one that glows', a heater with glowing elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as glow-er, something that glows, it describes a heater whose radiants glow red.

clue.text: Final outcome nothing very special

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
mega is slang for great or very special

explanation.surface: The final result turned out to be nothing very special.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end, the final outcome of things.

clue.text: Indian greeting one stealing inside the country's border

indicators.note: inside places the one stealing within the greeting

parts.note: 'How!' is the greeting given to Native Americans in old Hollywood westerns
to edge is to creep or steal along, so one who does that is an edger

explanation.surface: An Indian greets someone who is sneaking in across the nation's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stealing' means creeping, not theft.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgerow is the line of bushes forming a field boundary in the countryside.

clue.text: Vegetarians skipping starter eating lettuce tops for breakfast

indicators.note: eating means the shortened word swallows the lettuce
skipping starter means losing the first letter

parts.note: veggies is informal for vegetarians
cos is a variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: Vegetarians skip the starter and eat lettuce leaves for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipping starter' drops the opening V, leaving EGGIES, and 'eating' puts the lettuce inside. 'tops' are covers for boiled eggs, not lettuce tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg cosies are little knitted covers kept on top of boiled eggs at breakfast.

clue.text: Rider's retreat after publicity turned up compromising info

definitions.note: the definition is rider, with 's for is

indicators.note: after puts the retreat following the publicity

parts.note: an ad is publicity
a den is a private retreat

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: mud is damaging information slung at someone

explanation.surface: A rider's hideout comes to light after damaging publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' is not a horseman but an extra clause added to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an extra clause appended to a document, a supplement.

clue.text: Doctor with register including what's complete

parts.note: Doctor Who is the BBC science-fiction hero

indicators.note: including says the register holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a log is a record or register
eh? is a way of saying what?, and the 's joins it on

explanation.surface: A doctor whose register includes everything that is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Going the whole hog is an idiom for doing something completely, so the phrase means entire.

clue.text: Vet responsible for woman's scream

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
a scream is a hilarious person or thing, a riot

explanation.surface: A vet is to blame for a woman's screaming.
explanation.walkthrough: James Herriot was the author-vet of All Creatures Great and Small.
explanation.definitionFit: James Herriot was the famous Yorkshire vet who wrote about his practice.

clue.text: Grand-daughter holding mirror was yawning

indicators.note: holding means the G and D grip the mirror word between them

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
to mirror someone is to copy or ape them

explanation.surface: A granddaughter holding up a mirror was yawning.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits 'Grand-daughter' into two pieces, G and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to open the mouth wide, as one does in a yawn.

clue.text: After crack, stick needle in one's tongue

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the crack

parts.note: a crack is a joke, such as a pun
to jab is to stick a needle in
one is I, with 's for is

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a needle in their tongue after it cracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' means language, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and Punjabi is spoken in Pakistan and northern India.

clue.text: Split state's capital

parts.note: Split is a Croatian port city, so the state it is in is Croatia, and its capital is meant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a verb; it is the Croatian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Croatia, the country containing the port of Split.

clue.text: Fruit fool date and custard — or tapioca originally

parts.note: April Fool's day is the first of April, written Apr 1
the 1 of Apr 1 is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of each of the words custard, or and tapioca

explanation.surface: A dessert menu offering a fruit fool with dates and custard, or else tapioca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' looks like the pudding but is April Fool's day, written APR 1.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Reluctant to support Conservative ministers

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece supports another by sitting below it

parts.note: loth means reluctant

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to back the Conservative ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers' are clergymen, collectively 'the cloth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is a collective term for the clergy, those who minister.

clue.text: Moving letter's conclusion one cut, to paste

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted around into a new order
conclusion picks the final letter of the word letter

explanation.surface: Moving a letter's ending: one cut it out, then pasted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges R (the end of 'letter's') with ONE and CUT. 'cut, to paste' reads as editing text; 'paste' means to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste someone is slang for beating them soundly, the same as to thrash.

clue.text: Ready for the big game?

definitions.meaning: the ready is slang for cash
big game is large wild animals hunted for sport, such as this horned beast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready for the big game' reads as a team prepared for a match. RHINO is old British slang for money, like 'the ready'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old slang for money, the ready; it is also a large horned animal of big-game hunting.

clue.text: Recalled man in middle row with Spanish king

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the referee is the man in the middle of a match, the ref
a din is a noisy row
and means with, along with

explanation.surface: A man brought back into the middle row next to a Spanish monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand was the name of several Spanish kings, notably the husband of Isabella.

clue.text: They curb lunatic's bloodletting

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild people restrain a madman's act of bloodletting.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchery is savage, wholesale slaughter, the spilling of blood.

clue.text: Heavy Metal one's into repelled parent so

indicators.note: into puts the one inside the other pieces
repelled means driven back, so the words are read in reverse

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
taken as written
one is I, with 's for is

explanation.surface: A heavy metal fan has driven away a parent, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns parent and so together into OSMUM; 'into' puts I inside. 'Heavy Metal' looks like the music; it is the densest element.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, a very heavy metal.
